correctness.rationale: The graph is unambiguously specified as the 12-vertex line graph of the 3-cube. Least-uncovered recursion exhausts exactly 32 perfect matching facets; closure enumerates 1,429 augmented faces with f-vector (24,192,520,468,192,32). A pairwise-disjoint 693-pair toggle Morse matching is verified acyclic on all 4,992 complete Hasse incidences, leaving 43 critical two-cells and no other nonempty critical cells, and the empty face is paired. The resulting CW model has one zero-cell and 43 two-cells and thus gives the claimed integral wedge. A separately constructed full mod-two simplicial boundary calculation has ranks (23,169,308,160,32), implying only reduced degree-two rank 43. Forty-eight explicit cube automorphisms induce signed permutations of every original chain simplex. Exhaustive fixed-face Lefschetz traces form ten internally consistent signed-cycle classes with the stated trace values and their character sum 96. Rational homology is only in degree two, so those traces give the complete rational degree-two character and invariant rank two.

originality.rationale: No inspected publication or indexed scientific record implied the perfect-matching complex homotopy type or its B3 rational character for the cuboctahedral graph. The foundational paper studies hexagonal honeycomb regions, later perfect-matching classifications study polygon chains and ladders, and published ordinary cuboctahedral matching-complex homotopy concerns a strictly larger complex. A group representation computed for a cuboctahedral two-particle configuration space concerns another space with nonzero first homology, so is not a classification of this perfect-matching complex. Unindexed overlap remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently titled calculations could already contain the same homotopy type or symmetry character.
Two later perfect-matching graph-family papers were assessed only at abstract level; their explicitly stated graph families exclude the cuboctahedral graph.
No classification is claimed for arbitrary line graphs, for higher-dimensional cubes, or for integral symmetry modules.

value.rationale: The cuboctahedral graph is a canonical 12-vertex Archimedean solid graph and the line graph of the cube, with a natural perfect-matching extendability complex. Its integral homotopy type is a complete, previously unimplicated exact invariant that distinguishes all perfect-matching faces from the larger ordinary matching complex. Computing the full 10-class 48-element cube-symmetry character and finding two invariant generators provides significant structural data beyond a mere sphere multiplicity. The intrinsic object and symmetry are mathematically motivated; no arbitrary parameter cutoff, unsupported downstream claim, or infinite-family conjecture is used.
